meta.title: Piuma — an Instagram content engine with human approval
meta.description: A draft from a person or an agent, approval by a person, publishing via the official Instagram Platform API. Three languages, hash-chained audit, encrypted secrets.
meta.keywords: Piuma, Instagram automation, post scheduling, Instagram Platform API, content engine, Instagram Insights, Carbon Stealth
meta.ogAlt: Piuma — an Instagram content engine by Carbon Stealth VCC

hero.title: Every draft goes through a person.
hero.lead: An agent or a person writes the draft. A person approves it in the panel. Only then does Piuma publish. There is no hidden path by which a draft reaches Instagram on its own.
hero.note: Accounts are connected through Meta's official OAuth. Piuma does not create accounts — Meta's terms forbid that, and a person does it by hand.
hero.shotAlt: The Piuma dashboard: drafts awaiting review, upcoming posts, per-account quotas

proof.reviewBody: The role is reviewer or above, the session is live, and your own draft is never approved by you.
proof.langBody: Bulgarian, English and Italian — full mirrors, not a partial translation.
proof.auditBody: Every action carries an actor and an IP. Tampering with an old entry breaks the chain and shows.

how.title: Three steps, never a fourth
how.lead: A post always travels the same road. There is no mode in which a step is skipped.
how.step1Body: By a person in the panel or by an agent through a signed key. Both paths produce a draft — nothing more.
how.step2Body: The linter checks the text; a high-severity finding blocks approval and no route can step over it.
how.step3Body: A queue with retries, the account's quota, and the result comes back to the panel with the reason for any refusal.
how.guardTitle: And if the agent gets it wrong?
how.guardBody: It cannot. No approval route exists for an agent key — the permission isn't restricted, it simply isn't there.

panel.title: The panel is where a person decides
panel.lead: Everything in one load: what is waiting for review, what is scheduled, what failed and why.
panel.point1: State is a chip with an icon and a word — colour never carries meaning on its own.
panel.point2: Seven roles with clear rights; sessions live in the database and are revoked at once.
panel.point3: Two-factor sign-in with a code from an app (TOTP), no SMS.
panel.point4: Works with JavaScript off — the panel is server-rendered and depends on no script.
panel.shotAlt: The post list in Piuma with status chips: draft, approved, scheduled, published, rejected
panel.composeAlt: Writing a draft in Piuma: by hand on the left, model suggestions on the right

autopilot.title: An autopilot that writes — but never publishes
autopilot.lead: For managed pages Piuma prepares drafts to plan once a week and reads Instagram Insights to know what worked. Approval stays human.
autopilot.point1: The plan is yours: how many posts, the share of Reels, the hours, the content pillars, what to avoid.
autopilot.point2: It draws only from the brand's media library — it invents no material.
autopilot.point3: Metrics are pulled overnight and shown as a 30-day trend.
autopilot.shotAlt: A 30-day trend in Piuma: followers, reach, views and engaged accounts

security.title: Security is the foundation, not a layer on top
security.lead: The product holds other people's Instagram accounts. That is why each of these is required, not optional.
security.item1Body: An HMAC signature over method, path and body, a timestamp within ±300 s and a nonce against replay. The secret never travels.
security.item2Body: Instagram tokens, TOTP and agent keys use AES-256-GCM and never reach a log.
security.item3Title: An audit that cannot be rewritten
security.item3Body: The chain of hashes makes a quiet edit of an old entry impossible.
security.item4Title: Strict CSP and sessions in the database
security.item4Body: Scripts only with a nonce, no inline style at all. Sessions slide for 7 days with a 30-day ceiling and are revoked at once.
security.item5Body: No SMS second factor, no tokens in localStorage, a cookie with the __Host- prefix.
security.item6Title: The data sits in the EU
security.item6Body: Our own PostgreSQL on a European server. No hosted CMS between you and your accounts.

langs.title: The panel speaks the team's language
langs.body: Switch it from the bar and it stays remembered in the profile. Bulgarian is the source; English and Italian are full mirrors, and the test fails on a missing key.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.q1: Can Piuma create an Instagram account?
faq.a1: No. Meta's terms forbid automated account creation. The account is made by hand, switched to a professional one and connected through the official OAuth.
faq.q2: Can an agent publish on its own?
faq.a2: No. An agent key reaches a draft and no further. No approval route exists for such a key, so there is nothing to work around.
faq.q3: What happens if Instagram refuses a post?
faq.a3: The queue retries, and the reason is recorded on the post and shown in the panel together with the number of attempts.
faq.q4: Where do the performance numbers come from?
faq.a4: From Instagram Insights, synced overnight for the account and for every published piece of media. Piuma invents no metrics.
faq.a5: Yes. The panel is server-rendered; the single script carries a nonce and adds convenience, not function.
faq.a6: Seven roles with different rights. Approval takes reviewer or above, and a draft is never approved by its own author.

keys.title: Agent keys
keys.subtitle: Machine access for our agents. Requests are HMAC-signed (the secret never travels), with a timestamp and a nonce against replay. The scope is narrow by construction: an agent can read and create drafts — approval, scheduling and publishing do not exist for keys.
keys.created: Key “{name}” created — the secret is shown only now
keys.createdHint: Put them on the agent's machine in a file with mode 600 (e.g. /etc/piuma/agent.env) and hand them to tools/social/piuma.mjs. Never in a repo, a chat or a log.
keys.name: Name
